boards.title: 10 Late-Night Runs That Explain American University
boards.description: Late-night dining at American University centers on the Tenleytown corridor and reliable on-campus tunnel spots that fuel study sessions and social breaks.

cards.title: Wawa Tenleytown
cards.subtitle: 24-Hour Convenience Hub
cards.notes: Visit this 24/7 staple for custom hoagies and late-night snacks. It is a primary destination for students seeking food after campus dining halls close.
cards.short_summary: A 24-hour convenience store and deli located near the Tenleytown-AU Metro station.
cards.evidence_claim: Wawa at 4530 40th St NW is open 24 hours daily, providing freshly brewed coffee and built-to-order hoagies at all hours.
cards.source_title: 4530 40th st nw a - Wawa
cards.access_notes: Open 24/7 for walk-in service and online ordering.

cards.title: Steak 'n Egg Kitchen
cards.subtitle: Classic 24-Hour Greasy Spoon
cards.notes: Head to this iconic diner for breakfast platters and burgers at any hour. It has served as a late-night landmark for the AU community for decades.
cards.short_summary: A long-standing 24-hour diner in Tenleytown known for its All-American breakfast and burgers.
cards.evidence_claim: Osman & Joe's Steak 'n Egg Kitchen is a 24-hour restaurant located at 4700 Wisconsin Avenue, NW.
cards.source_title: Steak N Egg Diner Tenleytown | Toast
cards.access_notes: Open 24 hours daily for dine-in and takeout.

cards.title: Surfside Tenleytown
cards.subtitle: Late-Night Tacos and Tex-Mex
cards.notes: Stop by for Baja-style tacos and burritos. While the dining room closes earlier, the bar remains a late-night gathering spot for students.
cards.short_summary: A popular Tex-Mex restaurant in Tenleytown offering fresh tacos and a late-night bar atmosphere.
cards.evidence_claim: The Surfside Tenleytown location has a bar open until midnight daily, with a dining room open until 10 PM or 11 PM.
cards.source_title: Contact Us | Washington DC's Go To Tex Mex - Surfside DC
cards.access_notes: Bar open until midnight daily; dining room hours vary by day.

cards.title: Eagle Express
cards.subtitle: On-Campus Convenience Store
cards.notes: Grab snacks, drinks, and quick meals in the Lydecker Tunnel. This is the primary on-campus source for late-night essentials using EagleBucks.
cards.short_summary: A university-run convenience store located in the Lydecker Tunnel of the Butler Pavilion.
cards.evidence_claim: Eagle Express is located in the Lydecker Tunnel and typically operates until midnight during the academic semester.
cards.source_title: Shuttle Service and Dining Hours Update (February 12) - American University
cards.access_notes: Open until midnight during regular semester operations.

cards.title: Subway at AU
cards.subtitle: Late-Night Tunnel Subs
cards.notes: Order a custom sandwich late into the evening without leaving campus. It is one of the most reliable late-night food options in the Lydecker Tunnel.
cards.short_summary: A Subway franchise located on-campus within the Lydecker Tunnel.
cards.evidence_claim: The Subway at American University in the Lydecker Tunnel is documented to stay open until midnight during standard operating days.
cards.source_title: Shuttle Service and Dining Hours Update (February 12) - American University
cards.access_notes: Located in the Lydecker Tunnel; open until midnight.

cards.title: Qdoba Mexican Eats
cards.subtitle: Late-Night Burritos on Campus
cards.notes: Build your own burrito or bowl at this tunnel favorite. It serves as a popular late-night alternative to the main dining hall.
cards.short_summary: An on-campus Mexican fast-casual restaurant located in the Lydecker Tunnel.
cards.evidence_claim: The Qdoba at American University is listed with hours extending until midnight on certain weekdays.
cards.source_title: QDOBA Locations in Washington, DC | Mexican Food & Catering
cards.access_notes: Open until midnight on select days; check university dining calendar for seasonal changes.

cards.title: The Bridge Cafe
cards.subtitle: Student-Run Coffee and Community
cards.notes: Study or socialize at this student-run spot in Butler Pavilion. It offers coffee and pastries until 10 PM, bridging the gap between dinner and late-night.
cards.short_summary: A student-run coffee shop and community space located on the second floor of Butler Pavilion.
cards.evidence_claim: The Bridge Cafe is open Monday through Thursday until 10:00 PM, serving as a central gathering space for students.
cards.source_title: The Bridge Cafe: Home
cards.access_notes: Open until 10 PM Monday-Thursday; hours vary on weekends.

cards.title: The Diner
cards.subtitle: 24/7 Adams Morgan Classic
cards.notes: Take a short trip to Adams Morgan for this 24/7 institution. It is a favorite for students seeking a full diner menu in a lively neighborhood setting.
cards.short_summary: A 24-hour diner in the Adams Morgan neighborhood offering a wide range of American comfort food.
cards.evidence_claim: The Diner in Adams Morgan is open 24 hours a day, seven days a week, providing a reliable late-night dining option in DC.
cards.source_title: The Diner | Adams Morgan Partnership
cards.access_notes: Open 24/7 for dine-in and takeout.

cards.title: Muncheez Georgetown
cards.subtitle: Late-Night Lebanese Street Food
cards.notes: Enjoy shawarma and crepes until the early morning hours. This Georgetown spot is a popular late-night destination for students exploring the city.
cards.short_summary: A Lebanese restaurant in Georgetown known for being open late and serving authentic street food.
cards.evidence_claim: Muncheez in Georgetown is documented as being open until 1 AM to 3 AM on most nights.
cards.source_title: Contact — Muncheez Shawarma Washington DC Open Late
cards.access_notes: Open late for pickup and delivery; typically until 3 AM on weekends.

cards.title: District Taco
cards.subtitle: Yucatán-Style Late Dinner
cards.notes: Grab a quick taco or burrito before 9 PM. While not open past midnight, it serves as a primary late-dinner run for students in the Tenleytown area.
cards.short_summary: A popular local chain serving Yucatán-inspired Mexican food in Tenleytown.
cards.evidence_claim: District Taco Tenleytown is open daily from 10 AM to 9 PM, serving as a key early-late-night dining option.
cards.source_title: The Best Tacos in Tenleytown, Washington D.C. - District Taco
cards.access_notes: Open until 9 PM daily.

boards.title: What the Campus Tour Skips: 10 Places Students Share With Each Other
boards.description: Discover the functional study hubs, quiet lounges, and student-run spaces that define daily life at American University beyond the standard admissions path.

cards.title: 24/7 Main Floor Study Zone
cards.subtitle: Bender Library
cards.notes: Access the main floor 24/7 with a valid AU ID. It is the only campus space guaranteed open for late-night cramming after other floors close at midnight.
cards.short_summary: The only 24/7 study space on campus, located on the library's entry level.
cards.evidence_claim: Bender Library provides a 24/7 study space on the main floor for students with a current, valid AU ID.
cards.source_title: Bender Library Launches 24/7 Study Space | American University
cards.access_notes: Open 24/7 for students with AU ID; staff support ends at midnight.

cards.title: The Dav Student-Run Hub
cards.subtitle: School of International Service
cards.notes: Visit this nonprofit, student-staffed cafe for a relaxed atmosphere. It's a central meeting spot for SIS students and features a historic chapel plaque.
cards.short_summary: A student-staffed nonprofit coffee shop located in the SIS building atrium.
cards.evidence_claim: The Davenport Coffee Lounge is a nonprofit, student-staffed coffee shop located in the School of International Service.
cards.source_title: Davenport Coffee Lounge
cards.access_notes: Open Monday-Friday during academic terms; check site for seasonal hours.

cards.title: The Underground Grad Retreat
cards.subtitle: Between SIS and Bender Library
cards.notes: Use the tunnel between SIS and the Library to find this quiet, grad-only zone. It features group workrooms and a dedicated smart classroom.
cards.short_summary: A dedicated study and event space for graduate students located underground.
cards.evidence_claim: The GRC is a dedicated study space for graduate students accessible via the SIS building terrace or Bender Library lower level.
cards.source_title: Graduate Research Center (GRC) - American University
cards.access_notes: Restricted to graduate students; open during library circulation desk hours.

cards.title: Natural Light Study Nook
cards.subtitle: McKinley Building, 3rd Floor
cards.notes: Head to the top floor for booths and high-top tables. This area is known for its abundance of natural light and quiet, focused atmosphere.
cards.short_summary: A quiet lounge area on the third floor of the School of Communication building.
cards.evidence_claim: The third floor of McKinley features a hallway lounge and rooftop terrace used as student study spaces.
cards.source_title: McKinley Building - 3rd Floor - Hallway Lounge
cards.access_notes: Open during building hours; typically quietest during morning hours.

cards.title: Soundproof Practice Pods
cards.subtitle: Katzen Arts Center, Ground Floor
cards.notes: Find these small rooms along the ground floor hallway. They are primarily for music students but often available for anyone needing a sound-isolated space.
cards.short_summary: Individual music practice rooms located on the ground level of the arts center.
cards.evidence_claim: The Katzen Arts Center provides instructional and performance space, including music practice rooms on the ground floor.
cards.source_title: Katzen Arts Center | American University
cards.access_notes: Priority for music students; check door postings for reservations.

cards.title: The Tech-Focused Commons
cards.subtitle: Don Myers Technology & Innovation Building
cards.notes: Located on East Campus, these spaces are less crowded than the main library. Ideal for group projects requiring whiteboards and tech integration.
cards.short_summary: Modern student collaboration and study spaces in the STEM-focused DMTI building.
cards.evidence_claim: DMTI features student collaboration and study spaces and fosters a community among CS, Physics, and Math-Stat students.
cards.source_title: Labs and Research | American University
cards.access_notes: Accessible via AU shuttle or a short walk across Nebraska Avenue.

cards.title: The First Floor Landing
cards.subtitle: Mary Graydon Center, Room 102
cards.notes: A dedicated spot for off-campus students to rest between classes. It's centrally located near the main dining areas and student mailroom.
cards.short_summary: A lounge specifically designated for commuter students on the first floor of MGC.
cards.evidence_claim: The Mary Graydon Student Center includes a Commuter Lounge in Room 102 on the first floor.
cards.source_title: Student Center Directory | American University
cards.access_notes: Open during standard Student Center hours; available to all students.

cards.title: The Atrium Social Steps
cards.subtitle: School of International Service
cards.notes: Sit on the wide wooden steps in the SIS atrium to people-watch or study. This LEED-gold space is the architectural heart of the building.
cards.short_summary: Wide, tiered seating steps in the SIS atrium used for studying and socializing.
cards.evidence_claim: The SIS building features 'Spanish Stairs' in the atrium as a primary gathering and seating area.
cards.source_title: SIS Building - 1st Floor - Spanish Stairs
cards.access_notes: Publicly accessible during building hours; often hosts informal events.

cards.title: The Campus Makerspace
cards.subtitle: Don Myers Building, Room 101
cards.notes: Join this community for free to use 3D printers and laser cutters. It's open to any student with an AU ID, regardless of their major.
cards.short_summary: A digital fabrication and rapid prototyping space open to the entire AU community.
cards.evidence_claim: The Design and Build Lab (DaBL) is a free experimentation space in DMTI 101 for anyone with an active AUID.
cards.source_title: Labs and Research | American University
cards.access_notes: Membership is free; check website for training and orientation times.

cards.title: The SPA Social Hub
cards.subtitle: Kerwin Hall, 1st Floor
cards.notes: Use the lobby tables for quick meetings between School of Public Affairs classes. It's a high-traffic area perfect for networking with faculty and peers.
cards.short_summary: The central lobby and research center hub for the School of Public Affairs.
cards.evidence_claim: Kerwin Hall's first floor includes a lobby and research centers used by students for academic activities.
cards.source_title: Kerwin Hall Building - 1st Floor - Lobby
cards.access_notes: Open during standard academic building hours.

boards.title: Zero Dollars: 10 Hangs That Cost Nothing
boards.description: Explore American University's campus and surrounding areas with these social and study spots that require no admission or purchase.

cards.title: Art at the Katzen Center
cards.subtitle: Katzen Arts Center
cards.notes: Browse three floors of contemporary art and rotating exhibitions. Admission is always free for students and the public during museum hours.
cards.short_summary: A free contemporary art museum featuring regional and international works.
cards.evidence_claim: Admission to the AU Museum is free.
cards.source_title: Plan Your Visit | AU Museum | American University, Washington, DC
cards.access_notes: Open Wednesday through Sunday, 11:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m.

cards.title: Campus Arboretum Walk
cards.subtitle: Main Campus Grounds
cards.notes: Walk through a designated Level II arboretum featuring over 5,000 trees. The grounds are open to the public for self-guided tours at no cost.
cards.short_summary: A public garden and arboretum spanning the entire 84-acre campus.
cards.evidence_claim: AU is a designated arboretum and public garden with more than 2,000 trees.
cards.source_title: Community Relations | American University, Washington, DC
cards.access_notes: Publicly accessible campus grounds.

cards.title: Weekly Tea Time
cards.subtitle: Kay Spiritual Life Center
cards.notes: Join a long-standing AU tradition every Tuesday for free tea, cupcakes, and conversation. It is open to all members of the campus community.
cards.short_summary: A weekly social gathering with free refreshments for the AU community.
cards.evidence_claim: Join us in the Kay Spiritual Life Center every Tuesday between 2 and 3 pm for tea, cupcakes, conversation.
cards.source_title: Building Community and Finding Support | American University, Washington, DC
cards.access_notes: Tuesdays from 2:00 PM to 3:00 PM.

cards.title: 24/7 Study Sessions
cards.subtitle: Bender Library Main Floor
cards.notes: Access the main floor of the library at any hour for late-night study. Use your valid AU ID for entry after midnight.
cards.short_summary: A 24-hour study space available to students on the library's main floor.
cards.evidence_claim: After midnight, library users with a current, valid AU ID will only be able to access the main floor of the library.
cards.source_title: Bender Library Launches 24/7 Study Space | American University, Washington, D.C.
cards.access_notes: 24/7 access for students with AU ID; public hours vary.

cards.title: Hike the Glover Archbold Trail
cards.subtitle: Adjacent to Campus
cards.notes: Explore 183 acres of wooded trails directly bordering the campus. This National Park Service site offers free hiking access year-round.
cards.short_summary: A nearby forested park with trails connecting campus to the Potomac River.
cards.evidence_claim: Glover Archbold Park is a 183-acre park... Admission to the Arboretum and the museum is free of charge.
cards.source_title: Glover Archbold Park (U.S. National Park Service)
cards.access_notes: Open daily from dawn to dusk.

cards.title: Sustainable Atrium Lounge
cards.subtitle: SIS Building
cards.notes: Relax in the sunlit, LEED Gold-certified atrium. It serves as a public meeting place and study area for students and visitors.
cards.short_summary: A bright, eco-friendly gathering space within the SIS building.
cards.evidence_claim: The sunlit atrium provides a welcome meeting place for the School and its visitors.
cards.source_title: American University School of International Service - William McDonough + Partners
cards.access_notes: Open during building operating hours.

cards.title: Student Center Hangouts
cards.subtitle: Mary Graydon Center
cards.notes: Utilize various free social spaces like Clawed's Corner or the Commuter Lounge. These areas are designed for student socializing and relaxation.
cards.short_summary: Multiple dedicated lounge spaces for students within the main student hub.
cards.evidence_claim: MGSC has something for everyone... including Clawed's Corner Lounge and Commuter Lounge.
cards.source_title: Student Center Operations | American University, Washington, DC
cards.access_notes: Open daily; specific lounge hours may vary.

cards.title: Cheer on the Eagles
cards.subtitle: Reeves Athletic Complex
cards.notes: Attend home soccer games for free with a valid AU student ID. The field is a historic campus venue that has hosted international teams.
cards.short_summary: Free admission for AU students to regular season soccer matches.
cards.evidence_claim: Free Admission for AU Students... Men's Soccer and Women's Soccer at Reeves Field.
cards.source_title: Ticket Office - American University - AUEagles.com
cards.access_notes: Free for students with AU ID; public tickets required for some events.

cards.title: Outdoor Amphitheatre Hang
cards.subtitle: The Quad
cards.notes: Sit on the stone tiers of this outdoor venue for a quiet break or to catch free student-run events and performances.
cards.short_summary: A historic outdoor amphitheatre used for student events and relaxation.
cards.evidence_claim: The amphitheater was also a popular venue for concerts... AU greets new students with All-American Welcome here.
cards.source_title: All-American Welcome - Washington, DC
cards.access_notes: Open outdoor space.

cards.title: The Dav Social Space
cards.subtitle: School of International Service
cards.notes: Enjoy the cozy atmosphere of 'The Dav' without needing to buy a drink. It is a historic student-run space perfect for group meetings.
cards.short_summary: A student-staffed lounge and coffee shop with a rich campus history.
cards.evidence_claim: The Davenport Chapel was converted into the Davenport Memorial Lounge, a place for SIS students to study, read and meet.
cards.source_title: About — THE DAV - Davenport Coffee Lounge
cards.access_notes: Open during academic semesters; hours vary.

boards.title: Claimed by 9am: 10 Study Spots Worth Showing Up Early For
boards.description: From silent library floors to sun-drenched atriums, American University offers a variety of environments for focused work and collaborative projects.

cards.title: The Silent Floor
cards.subtitle: Bender Library
cards.notes: Adhere to the strict no-talking policy on this floor. It is ideal for deep focus and individual work in a completely silent environment.
cards.short_summary: The designated silent floor of the main campus library, featuring individual carrels and a strict noise policy.
cards.evidence_claim: The second floor of the library is a Silent floor, where whispering and talking are not permitted.
cards.source_title: Where can I find a quiet study space? - University Library FAQs
cards.access_notes: Open to all AU students with a valid ID; the first floor is available 24/7 during semesters.

cards.title: The Spanish Steps
cards.subtitle: School of International Service
cards.notes: Grab a coffee from the Davenport Lounge and find a spot on these wide wooden steps for casual reading or laptop work.
cards.short_summary: A tiered seating area in the LEED Gold-certified SIS building atrium, popular for social and casual study.
cards.evidence_claim: Students study on the Spanish Steps in the SIS building, which is the heart of the school.
cards.source_title: The Eagle's guide to AU's best study spots
cards.access_notes: Publicly accessible during building hours; located near the Davenport Coffee Lounge.

cards.title: The SOC Sky Lounge
cards.subtitle: McKinley Building
cards.notes: Utilize the booths and high-top tables on the top floor of the School of Communication for a bright, quiet workspace.
cards.short_summary: A modern lounge area with abundant natural light and a mix of seating types for quiet individual study.
cards.evidence_claim: On the third floor of McKinley, there is a collection of lounge chairs, booths and high top tables, perfect for every type of studier.
cards.source_title: The Eagle's guide to AU's best study spots
cards.access_notes: Open to all students during building hours; features extensive natural light.

cards.title: The Innovation Hub
cards.subtitle: Don Myers Technology and Innovation Building
cards.notes: Head to the East Campus for these high-tech spaces that are often less crowded than main campus locations.
cards.short_summary: Modern study and collaboration areas located in the LEED Gold-certified technology building on East Campus.
cards.evidence_claim: DMTI features student collaboration and study spaces and fosters a community among CS, Physics, and Math-Stat students.
cards.source_title: Labs and Research | American University, Washington, DC
cards.access_notes: Accessible to students with AU ID; located on Nebraska Avenue across from main campus.

cards.title: The Science Commons
cards.subtitle: Hall of Science
cards.notes: Use the casual seating and collaborative tables in this new facility for group projects or science-focused study.
cards.short_summary: A contemporary workspace within the Hall of Science designed for student connectivity and group work.
cards.evidence_claim: The Hall of Science also provides students with collaborative workspaces and casual seating to study and enjoy.
cards.source_title: Hall of Science - Washington, DC - American University
cards.access_notes: Open during academic building hours; located near the Beeghly Chemistry Building.

cards.title: The Creative Atrium
cards.subtitle: Battelle-Tompkins Building
cards.notes: Join a group at one of the large tables in this first-floor atrium for a collaborative and artistic atmosphere.
cards.short_summary: A central campus atrium known for its large tables and suitability for group collaboration.
cards.evidence_claim: The Battelle atrium, located on the first floor of the Battelle-Tompkins Building, is a place to be collaborative.
cards.source_title: The Eagle's guide to AU's best study spots
cards.access_notes: Publicly accessible during building hours; tables can fit up to six people.

cards.title: The Law Library Retreat
cards.subtitle: Washington College of Law
cards.notes: Reserve one of the 22 study rooms on the Tenley Campus for a private, professional environment away from the main quad.
cards.short_summary: Private study rooms located on the 2nd and 3rd floors of the law library on the Tenleytown campus.
cards.evidence_claim: There are 22 study rooms located on the 2nd & 3rd floors of the library and on the Terrace level in the commons.
cards.source_title: Seat Availability - LibCal - American University Washington College of Law
cards.access_notes: Reservations required via LibCal; primarily for WCL students but accessible to the AU community.

cards.title: The Arts Rotunda
cards.subtitle: Katzen Arts Center
cards.notes: Find a seat in the rotunda or the second-floor lounge areas for a study session surrounded by contemporary art.
cards.short_summary: A visually inspiring study environment within the university's premier arts and museum complex.
cards.evidence_claim: The Katzen Arts Center provides state-of-the-art instructional, exhibition, and performance space for all the arts disciplines.
cards.source_title: Katzen Arts Center | American University, Washington, DC
cards.access_notes: Open during museum and building hours; features various seating nooks.

cards.title: The Grad Student Sanctuary
cards.subtitle: Lower Level, Bender Library/SIS
cards.notes: Graduate students can access this dedicated space for quiet research and collaborative group work.
cards.short_summary: A dedicated study and event space for graduate students located between the Library and SIS building.
cards.evidence_claim: The Graduate Research Center (GRC) is a study and event space dedicated to graduate students.
cards.source_title: Does the Library provide private spaces for groups or individuals?
cards.access_notes: Restricted to graduate students with AU ID; accessible from the library lower level.

cards.title: The MGC Booths
cards.subtitle: Mary Graydon Center
cards.notes: Look for the individual sound-dampening study booths scattered throughout the student center for private calls or focused work.
cards.short_summary: Individual study pods and booths located within the main student union building.
cards.evidence_claim: The individual sound / study booths they have all around MGC are great for Zoom calls and private study.
cards.source_title: Best places to Zoom on campus? : r/AmericanU
cards.access_notes: Open during MGC building hours; first-come, first-served basis.

boards.title: 10 Blocks Off Campus, One Reason Each
boards.description: Explore the essential streets and corridors surrounding American University, from the commercial hubs of Tenleytown to the quiet residential blocks of Spring Valley.

cards.title: The Tenleytown Hub
cards.subtitle: Wisconsin Avenue Corridor
cards.notes: Visit the primary commercial strip for students to find essentials at Target, Whole Foods, and local favorites like Z-Burger near the Tenleytown-AU Metro station.
cards.short_summary: The main commercial corridor serving the AU community with retail and dining.
cards.evidence_claim: Wisconsin Avenue is the primary commercial corridor for American University students, featuring the Tenleytown-AU Metro station and major retailers like Target and Whole Foods.
cards.source_title: Housing Guide - American University
cards.access_notes: Accessible via the AU Shuttle or a 15-minute walk from the main campus.

cards.title: Embassy Row Access
cards.subtitle: Massachusetts Avenue Corridor
cards.notes: Walk southeast from campus to pass numerous international embassies and reach the Spring Valley shopping center for local dining and services.
cards.short_summary: A scenic corridor home to international embassies and the Spring Valley shopping area.
cards.evidence_claim: Massachusetts Avenue NW is the main thoroughfare for AU, known for its proximity to 'Embassy Row' and the Spring Valley shopping center.
cards.source_title: DC Has It All | American University
cards.access_notes: The main campus entrance is located directly on this avenue.

cards.title: The Neighborhood Nook
cards.subtitle: New Mexico Avenue Corridor
cards.notes: Stop by the 3201 New Mexico Avenue complex to visit Wagshal's Deli or grab a coffee at Starbucks in a quiet residential setting.
cards.short_summary: A quiet corridor featuring student-frequented eateries and university offices.
cards.evidence_claim: New Mexico Avenue hosts university administrative offices and popular student spots like Wagshal's and Starbucks.
cards.source_title: Off Campus Eaglebucks Merchants | American University
cards.access_notes: Located south of the main campus near the Nebraska Avenue intersection.

cards.title: The Campus Connector
cards.subtitle: Nebraska Avenue Corridor
cards.notes: Follow this route to connect between the main campus and the Washington College of Law at the Tenley Campus.
cards.short_summary: A key transit route connecting AU's main and Tenley campuses.
cards.evidence_claim: Nebraska Avenue NW serves as the primary link between AU's main campus and the Tenley Campus/Washington College of Law.
cards.source_title: Visiting Campus | American University
cards.access_notes: Major bus routes and the AU shuttle frequently travel this corridor.

cards.title: Law School Gateway
cards.subtitle: Yuma Street Corridor
cards.notes: Use the Yuma Street entrance for direct access to the Washington College of Law and its modern academic facilities.
cards.short_summary: A quiet street providing the primary entrance to the AU Washington College of Law.
cards.evidence_claim: Yuma Street NW provides a major entrance point to the AU Washington College of Law Tenley Campus.
cards.source_title: General Directions and Parking | Washington College of Law
cards.access_notes: The Yuma entrance is the primary pedestrian access from the Tenleytown Metro.

cards.title: The Shuttle Stop
cards.subtitle: Albemarle Street Corridor
cards.notes: Catch the AU Shuttle at the corner of 40th and Albemarle, right in front of the Whole Foods, for a quick ride back to campus.
cards.short_summary: A key transit point for students using the university shuttle system.
cards.evidence_claim: The AU Shuttle stop for the Tenleytown-AU Metro station is located at the intersection of 40th and Albemarle Streets.
cards.source_title: AU Shuttle | American University
cards.access_notes: Shuttles run frequently between this point and the main campus.

cards.title: Spring Valley Border
cards.subtitle: 48th Street Corridor
cards.notes: Explore the edge of the Spring Valley neighborhood, where the university's Spring Valley Building houses the Abroad at AU office.
cards.short_summary: A residential street bordering the campus and housing university offices.
cards.evidence_claim: 48th Street NW borders the Spring Valley neighborhood and the AU Spring Valley Building.
cards.source_title: Contact Us - Abroad at AU | American University
cards.access_notes: A short walk from the Katzen Arts Center across Massachusetts Avenue.

cards.title: Student Living Row
cards.subtitle: Van Ness Street Corridor
cards.notes: Walk through this residential area where many upperclassmen and law students find off-campus apartments within walking distance of campus.
cards.short_summary: A popular residential street for off-campus student housing.
cards.evidence_claim: Van Ness Street is a primary residential area for AU students living off-campus in the Tenleytown and Van Ness neighborhoods.
cards.source_title: Housing Guide - American University
cards.access_notes: Connects the main campus area to the Van Ness-UDC Metro station area.

cards.title: The Campus Crossroads
cards.subtitle: Ward Circle District
cards.notes: Navigate this major traffic circle where Massachusetts and Nebraska Avenues meet, serving as the primary landmark for the university's main entrance.
cards.short_summary: The iconic traffic circle and landmark at the entrance of American University.
cards.evidence_claim: Ward Circle is the central landmark and intersection at the main entrance of American University.
cards.source_title: Visiting Campus | American University
cards.access_notes: Pedestrian crosswalks allow access to the campus gates from all sides of the circle.

cards.title: The Law School Link
cards.subtitle: Tenley Circle District
cards.notes: Pass through this circle to reach the Tenley Campus or the historic St. Ann's Church, a prominent neighborhood landmark.
cards.short_summary: A historic traffic circle adjacent to the AU Tenley Campus.
cards.evidence_claim: Tenley Circle is a major intersection adjacent to the AU Washington College of Law and the Tenleytown commercial area.
cards.source_title: General Directions and Parking | Washington College of Law
cards.access_notes: Located at the intersection of Wisconsin Avenue, Nebraska Avenue, and Yuma Street.

boards.title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
boards.description: From primal screams on the quad to rubbing the talons of a bronze eagle for luck, American University's traditions reflect its unique identity in the heart of the nation's capital.

cards.title: The Quad Scream
cards.subtitle: A Primal Finals Ritual
cards.notes: Join hundreds of students on the quad at 11:59 PM the night before finals begin to release stress with a collective one-minute primal scream.
cards.short_summary: A collective one-minute scream held at midnight on the quad to relieve stress before final exams.
cards.evidence_claim: The Quad Scream is a time-honored AU tradition that takes place on the Quad each year on the eve of finals week at precisely 11:59 PM.
cards.source_title: AU Traditions | American University, Washington, DC
cards.access_notes: Occurs annually on the night before finals week begins; open to all students.

cards.title: Rubbing the Eagle Talon
cards.subtitle: For Good Luck and Spirit
cards.notes: Rub the talon of the bronze eagle statue outside Bender Arena during Convocation to ensure good luck throughout your academic career.
cards.short_summary: A good-luck ritual where students rub the talon of the eagle statue outside Bender Arena during major ceremonies.
cards.evidence_claim: New Eagles proudly rub the talon of the Eagle statue, located outside of Bender Arena, as they enter Convocation for good luck.
cards.source_title: AU Traditions | American University, Washington, DC
cards.access_notes: Statue is accessible 24/7 outside the arena entrance.

cards.title: Thank Clawed It's Wednesday
cards.subtitle: Weekly Mid-Week Spirit
cards.notes: Wear your AU red, white, and blue every Wednesday to join Clawed the Eagle for music, activities, and community on the quad.
cards.short_summary: A weekly spirit event featuring the mascot, music, and student activities on the campus quad.
cards.evidence_claim: Thank Clawed It's Wednesday transforms the Quad into a vibrant community gathering space each week from 1:00 PM to 3:00 PM.
cards.source_title: Thank Clawed | American University, Washington, DC
cards.access_notes: Held weekly on Wednesdays from 1:00 PM to 3:00 PM during the academic year.

cards.title: Founders Day Ball
cards.subtitle: A Formal City-Wide Celebration
cards.notes: Attend this massive formal dance held at iconic D.C. venues like the Smithsonian to celebrate the university's February charter date.
cards.short_summary: An annual formal ball held in February at various prominent Washington, D.C. museums and landmarks.
cards.evidence_claim: The Founders Day Ball is one of the signature events of modern Founders Day, often held at venues like the National Air and Space Museum.
cards.source_title: Founders Day | AU Library Archives
cards.access_notes: Annual event in February; requires ticket purchase for students.

cards.title: The Wonk Identity
cards.subtitle: Embracing the Policy Expert
cards.notes: Identify as a 'Wonk'—a term AU reclaimed to describe students who are smart, passionate, and focused on creating meaningful change.
cards.short_summary: A unique branding and identity movement where AU students embrace the term 'wonk' to signify expertise and passion.
cards.evidence_claim: The WONK campaign launched in 2010 to define the AU community as smart, passionate, focused, and engaged individuals.
cards.source_title: Wonk campaign | American University, Washington, DC
cards.access_notes: A campus-wide cultural identity visible through apparel and events.

cards.title: Late Night Breakfast
cards.subtitle: Welcome Week Fuel
cards.notes: Kick off the semester at TDR with breakfast for dinner, featuring pancakes and eggs served late at night during Welcome Week.
cards.short_summary: A popular Welcome Week event where the main dining hall serves breakfast favorites late into the night.
cards.evidence_claim: Late-Night Breakfast involves a special treat—breakfast for dinner—offering students a chance to savor favorites in the evening.
cards.source_title: AU Traditions | American University, Washington, DC
cards.access_notes: Typically held from 10 PM to 12 AM during the first week of the fall semester.

cards.title: Tea Time at Kay
cards.subtitle: The Flaming Cupcake Ritual
cards.notes: Visit the Kay Center on Tuesdays for free tea and cupcakes, a tradition designed to foster casual fellowship across all faiths.
cards.short_summary: A weekly interfaith gathering featuring free tea and cupcakes to build community on campus.
cards.evidence_claim: The Office of the University Chaplain hosts a tea time at Kay Spiritual Life Center on Tuesdays from 2 to 3pm.
cards.source_title: Events and Programs at Kay Spiritual Life Center
cards.access_notes: Tuesdays from 2:00 PM to 3:00 PM during the academic year.

cards.title: Jazz in the Katz
cards.subtitle: Artistic Welcome
cards.notes: Experience local D.C. jazz bands in the modern Katzen Arts Center during the first week of classes to celebrate the city's musical history.
cards.short_summary: An annual jazz performance held at the Katzen Arts Center to welcome students to the D.C. music scene.
cards.evidence_claim: Jazz in the Katz began in 2018 and is hosted by the Center for Student Involvement during All American Welcome.
cards.source_title: AU Traditions | American University, Washington, DC
cards.access_notes: Held annually during All-American Welcome week in August.

cards.title: CultureFest
cards.subtitle: BIPOC Community Celebration
cards.notes: Celebrate AU's diverse student body with food, music, and activities from over 20 cultural organizations on the quad.
cards.short_summary: A major outdoor festival celebrating cultural diversity and student organizations on the campus quad.
cards.evidence_claim: Culturefest, a BIPOC celebration, has been an AU tradition since 2017, featuring 20-30 cultural organizations on the Quad.
cards.source_title: AU Traditions | American University, Washington, DC
cards.access_notes: Held annually during All-American Welcome week.

cards.title: Convocation Pinning
cards.subtitle: Symbol of Belonging
cards.notes: Receive your official AU pin during the New Student Convocation ceremony to mark your formal entry into the Eagle community.
cards.short_summary: A ceremony where new students receive a university pin to symbolize their membership in the AU community.
cards.evidence_claim: The convocation pin serves as a symbol of unity and pride, creating a sense of belonging among new students.
cards.source_title: AU Traditions | American University, Washington, DC
cards.access_notes: Occurs during the New Student Convocation ceremony in August.

boards.title: Your First Weekend at American University, Shared as Cards
boards.description: Build a plausible under-21-safe first-weekend sequence, not a ranking. Give each card one role in the sequence and use evergreen places or recurring behaviors rather than one-time events. Be conservative about hours, access, and travel time unless directly sourced.

cards.title: Unpack at South Campus
cards.subtitle: Friday Morning Arrival
cards.notes: Check into your new home at Letts Hall. Meet your RA and start unpacking before the weekend festivities begin.
cards.short_summary: The primary residence hall for many incoming first-year students during move-in weekend.
cards.evidence_claim: New students living on campus typically check into Letts Hall during the initial move-in period.
cards.source_title: After Hours & Weekend Activities | School of Communication
cards.access_notes: Restricted to residents with AU ID card access.

cards.title: First Meal at TDR
cards.subtitle: Friday Lunch Break
cards.notes: Head to the basement of Mary Graydon Center for your first meal. Try the omelet station, a student favorite.
cards.short_summary: The main all-you-care-to-eat dining hall on campus, commonly referred to as TDR.
cards.evidence_claim: TDR is the primary dining location for students and is open for breakfast, lunch, and dinner during orientation.
cards.source_title: Dining Calendar and Hours | American University
cards.access_notes: Open daily; lunch typically 11:00 AM - 2:00 PM. Requires meal plan or payment.

cards.title: Ride the Blue Route
cards.subtitle: Friday Afternoon Exploration
cards.notes: Board the shuttle at Letts/Anderson to reach Tenleytown. It is the easiest way to connect to the DC Metro.
cards.short_summary: The university's free shuttle service connecting the main campus to the Tenleytown-AU Metro station.
cards.evidence_claim: The Blue Route shuttle runs between Main Campus and Tenleytown Metro, with weekend hours starting at 8:00 AM.
cards.source_title: AU Shuttle Services | American University
cards.access_notes: Free for students with AU ID. Runs until 11:30 PM on weekends.

cards.title: Late Night at the Rec
cards.subtitle: Friday Night Social
cards.notes: Join hundreds of classmates for games and music. It is a high-energy way to meet people on your first night.
cards.short_summary: The university's main athletic arena, which hosts large-scale student social events during orientation.
cards.evidence_claim: Late Night at the Rec is a featured All-American Welcome event held at Bender Arena from 9:00 PM to 11:00 PM.
cards.source_title: All-American Welcome | American University
cards.access_notes: Event typically runs 9:00 PM - 11:00 PM during welcome week.

cards.title: New Student Convocation
cards.subtitle: Saturday Morning Tradition
cards.notes: Gather with your entire class for the official welcome ceremony. It is the first of two times your whole class meets.
cards.short_summary: The central campus green space where major university ceremonies and traditions take place.
cards.evidence_claim: New Student Convocation is a mandatory tradition held on the Quad to officially welcome the incoming class.
cards.source_title: AU Traditions | American University
cards.access_notes: Open public space; ceremony time is typically Friday or Saturday morning of welcome week.

cards.title: Explore the AU Museum
cards.subtitle: Saturday Afternoon Culture
cards.notes: Walk across Mass Ave to see contemporary art. The museum is free for students and offers a quiet break from the Quad.
cards.short_summary: A 130,000 square foot arts complex housing the American University Museum and performing arts spaces.
cards.evidence_claim: The AU Museum at the Katzen Arts Center is open Wednesday through Sunday, 11:00 AM to 4:00 PM.
cards.source_title: Plan Your Visit | AU Museum
cards.access_notes: Open 11:00 AM - 4:00 PM. Admission is free.

cards.title: Late Night Breakfast
cards.subtitle: Saturday Night Feast
cards.notes: Enjoy pancakes and eggs for dinner at TDR. This long-standing tradition is a favorite for meeting new friends.
cards.short_summary: A popular orientation event where breakfast food is served late at night in the dining hall.
cards.evidence_claim: Late-Night Breakfast is a long-standing tradition co-hosted by AU Dining, typically held from 10:00 PM to 12:00 AM.
cards.source_title: The Eagle's guide to 'Welcome Week at Night' events
cards.access_notes: Typically held 10:00 PM - 12:00 AM during Welcome Week.

cards.title: Reflect at the Labyrinth
cards.subtitle: Sunday Morning Quiet
cards.notes: Take a mindful walk on the path in front of Kay Spiritual Life Center. It is a peaceful spot to de-stress.
cards.short_summary: An outdoor meditative path located directly in front of the Kay Spiritual Life Center on the main quad.
cards.evidence_claim: The University Labyrinth is an outdoor space for reflection and meditation located in front of the Kay Spiritual Life Center.
cards.source_title: The University Labyrinth | American University
cards.access_notes: Outdoor space accessible 24/7.

cards.title: Walk the Arboretum
cards.subtitle: Sunday Afternoon Stroll
cards.notes: Explore the 84-acre campus garden. Look for the Franklin Tree near McCabe Hall, a rare species with a storied history.
cards.short_summary: The entire 84-acre American University campus is a designated and award-winning arboretum.
cards.evidence_claim: The AU Arboretum features over 5,000 trees and 500 species, including the Franklin Tree on the south side of McCabe Hall.
cards.source_title: Arboretum and Gardens | American University
cards.access_notes: Campus grounds are open to the public during daylight hours.

cards.title: Movie Under the Stars
cards.subtitle: Sunday Night Finale
cards.notes: Bring a blanket to the Quad for an outdoor film screening. It is the perfect way to end your first weekend at AU.
cards.short_summary: The central quadrangle where outdoor movies are screened for students during the first weeks of the semester.
cards.evidence_claim: Outdoor movies are a recurring Welcome Week event held on the Quad, often starting around 9:00 PM.
cards.source_title: Thank Clawed | American University
cards.access_notes: Events typically start at 9:00 PM. Open to all students.
